title: Tenant Residency Assertion Rotation and Proof Lifecycle
creator: Maya Thompson
description:
Background: Dedicated tenants require immutable, verifiable residency assertions for compliance audits. Current artifacts are generated ad-hoc and stored in opaque blobs; we need a structured lifecycle that covers creation, cryptographic signing, rotation of signing keys, retention/purge policies, and automated export bundles for auditors.

Goal: Implement a full proof lifecycle for tenant residency assertions that is auditable, automatable, and integrates with KMS/HSM for key management. The system should produce time-bound signed assertions, maintain a provable chain-of-custody, support scheduled key rotation without breaking historical verification, and provide retention controls tied to tenant contracts.

Scope:
- Assertion format: canonical JSON-LD payload with fields: tenant_id, node_ids, geo_zone, generation_time, ttl, provenance_refs, sequence_number, signer_key_id, and signature (JWS compact).
- Signing: integrate with customer-specific KMS keys (supported: AWS KMS, Google Cloud KMS, and on-prem HSM via PKCS#11). Signatures must be verifiable offline using public key exports.
- Key rotation: implement key rollover metadata so verifiers can reconstruct signing key history. Support overlapping validity windows and publish a signed key-history manifest.
- Retention policy enforcement: tie assertion TTLs to tenant retention settings; implement automated purging pipeline that emits deletion proof records for auditors.
- Export bundles: create tamper-evident ZIP bundles containing assertions, key-history manifest, export manifest, and a top-level signed index for auditors. Bundles must be generatable on-demand and scheduled (daily/weekly).
- API: provide REST endpoints to: 1) request a fresh assertion, 2) retrieve historical assertions, 3) request an export bundle, and 4) query key history and verification metadata. Endpoints must be rate-limited and logged.
- Observability: track assertion generation latency, signing failures, export job success rate, bundle size, and verification errors. Expose metrics and per-tenant dashboards.

Design notes & trade-offs:
- JWS vs custom signature: choose JWS (RFC7515) for ecosystem tooling and offline verification. Use detached payloads for compactness when storing large caches.
- Key storage: prefer cloud KMS for hosted customers; provide HSM adapters for Private deployments. Key rotation logic and manifests live in the control plane but signing occurs in the region-resident signing agent for Dedicated.
- Retention enforcement: soft-delete + cryptographic deletion proofs vs immediate shred. We will produce deletion proof records and allow configurable purge windows to satisfy regulatory hold requests.
- Performance: signing is CPU bound; use batching for high-throughput assertion generation and a small worker pool per region to avoid GC/latency spikes.

Implementation plan (milestones):
1) Data model and schema (this ticket) — define canonical assertion JSON and manifest schema.
2) KMS/HSM adapter + local signing agent prototype — PoC using AWS KMS and SoftHSM.
3) Key-history manifest and rotation protocol — implement manifest generation and verifier logic.
4) Export bundle assembler and on-demand API + scheduled job runner.
5) Retention/purge pipeline with deletion proof generation.
6) Dashboarding, alerts, and e2e tests, followed by an internal beta with two Dedicated tenants.

Acceptance criteria:
- Generate and sign assertions end-to-end (control plane + regional signer) with verifiable JWS signatures.
- Verify historical signatures after simulated key rotations using key-history manifest.
- Produce a signed export bundle containing >30 days of assertions and pass an internal verification tool.
- Retention purge removes assertion blobs and records deletion proofs; proof can be validated by the verification tool.
- Metrics & dashboards surface generation failures and export job health.

Security considerations:
- Enforce least privilege for signing agents. Keys must never leave KMS/HSM in plaintext.
- All transport uses mTLS. Export bundles are encrypted at rest using a customer- or platform-managed envelope key.
- Audit logs must include signer_key_id and sequence_number for non-repudiation.

Rollout plan:
- Alpha: internal test tenants (dev-only keys) — 2 weeks.
- Beta: two Dedicated customers on a private plane with opt-in entitlements — 4 weeks.
- GA: scheduled after passing audit-run and security review — target release dedicated-2026.03.

Rollbacks & migration: assertions are append-only; if bugs occur, we can pause export generation and rotate to a fallback signing key while maintaining key-history manifest to preserve verifiability.

Future work: add notarization integration (e.g., sigstore) and a searchable evidence index for legal discovery.
